title: Property taxes, insurance, PMI, and escrow

national.document: 2021 National Standards for Personal Financial Education (CEE and Jump$tart)
national.learning_target: Calculate the full cost of homeownership including taxes, insurance, and mortgage insurance
national.outcome_code_status: to verify against the official document

new_jersey.performance_expectation_status: strand-level alignment; individual 9.1.12 performance expectations to verify

sources.claim: Mortgage payments often include principal, interest, property taxes, and homeowners insurance (PITI); private mortgage insurance is usually required with less than 20% down on a conventional loan.
sources.verification: Not re-verified online: the authoring environment could not open this site on 2026-10-12. A reviewer must confirm the claim against the source before import.

sections.skill: Calculate a full monthly housing payment including taxes, insurance, and mortgage insurance

questions.prompt: A home's property tax is $6,000 a year. How much is that per month?
questions.intro: Monthly housing costs for owners usually include PITI: Principal, Interest, property Taxes, and homeowners Insurance. Taxes and insurance are often billed yearly but budgeted (and often paid) monthly.
questions.topic: Property taxes, insurance, PMI, and escrow
sources: CFPB (Buying a House): Mortgage payments often include principal, interest, property taxes, and homeowners insurance (PITI); private mortgage insurance is usually required with less than 20% down on a conventional loan. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/)

questions.prompt: Principal and interest: $1,516.96. Property tax: $500 a month. Homeowners insurance: $150 a month. What is the monthly PITI?
questions.intro: PITI = principal and interest + monthly property taxes + monthly homeowners insurance.
questions.topic: Property taxes, insurance, PMI, and escrow

questions.prompt: Lenders usually require private mortgage insurance (PMI) on a conventional loan when the down payment is under 20%. What does PMI protect?

choices.text: The house against damage from a fire
The lender, if the borrower defaults

questions.correct_answer: The lender, if the borrower defaults
questions.intro: PMI is insurance that protects the LENDER (not you) if you stop paying. It is usually required on conventional loans with less than 20% down and can typically be removed once you reach enough equity.

questions.prompt: An escrow account is…

choices.text: a savings account for the down payment
an account the lender uses to pay taxes and insurance
the seller's profit from the sale
a fee for the real estate agent

questions.correct_answer: an account the lender uses to pay taxes and insurance
questions.intro: Many lenders collect a monthly amount for taxes and insurance along with the mortgage payment and hold it in escrow, then pay those bills when due.
questions.feedback: Escrow collects and pays taxes and insurance on your behalf.
